news.title: FIFA faces fresh transparency calls after retreat on World Cup sell-off plan
news.lede: FIFA faced renewed calls for transparency on Saturday after it abruptly shelved plans to sell a stake in the commercial rights to the World Cup, a proposal that triggered fierce ‌backlash from regional confederations that said they had been blindsided. The swift reversal has exposed growing unease within world soccer over FIFA President Gianni Infantino's leadership style, with football officials demanding greater oversight of decisions that could reshape the governance and commercial future ‌of the sport. The backlash has also raised questions about Infantino's political capital as ⁠he prepares to seek another term in office. FIFA's plan was to raise up to $4.2 ⁠billion by selling about ⁠a 20% stake to private investors in a new unit that would run FIFA events, including the ‌World Cup.

news.title: Is Concacaf ready to make challenge to FIFA presidency?
news.lede: When news broke that FIFA was scrapping its commercialization plans, there was rampant celebration globally. Now, though, there is likely to be a fallout from the proposal and its driver, FIFA president Gianni Infantino. Within a statement released by Concacaf, it sure seems like the organization could be making a run at the throne: > Concacaf and its 41 Member Associations welcome the withdrawal of the proposed FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE). > The Confederation also commends its 41 Member Associations and the wider football family for the courage and unity they have shown this week.

news.title: FIFA’s Infantino Scraps World Cup Investment Plan. But Is It Too Little, Too Late?
news.lede: FIFA President Gianni Infantino said Friday that football's international governing body would scrap plans to sell private investors a stake in a new commercial venture tied to the World Cup. The pivot came after widespread backlash and vows from all 55 members of UEFA (the Union of European Football Associations) to boycott future FIFA competitions if the plans went through. “Having listened carefully to all the views, it has become clear that the project has created divisions of a nature that, regardless of the level of support, are no longer in the interest of the objective set out in the first place,” Infantino said in a statement. “Our purpose has always been — and will always be — to unite and improve.

news.title: UEFA will boycott FIFA tournaments if Gianni Infantino continues with plans to sell off stake in World Cup
news.lede: UEFA will boycott FIFA tournaments if Gianni Infantino goes ahead with his proposal to sell off a stake in the World Cup. The decision was taken at an emergency meeting of all of UEFA's 55 member associations on Thursday afternoon, with a 55-0 vote. In a statement released on Thursday afternoon, UEFA said: "We unanimously and unequivocally reject FIFA's proposal to transfer ownership interests in the World Cup and other FIFA competitions to private investors." Q&A: Why is UEFA boycotting FIFA tournaments and can it stop Gianni Infantino?

news.title: FIFA presidency under fire as CONCACAF, UEFA slam Infantino over scrapped World Cup investment plan
news.lede: CONCACAF has called for a "comprehensive reckoning" with Gianni Infantino's leadership of FIFA, joining UEFA in criticising the World Cup organiser's handling of an aborted plan to allow private investment in football's showpiece tournament.North and Central American football's governing body issued the rebuke in a statement on Saturday, a day after Infantino abandoned the controversial proposal amid fierce global backlash." This recent unilateral and egregious act of poor governance and leadership follows a pattern of missteps and similar behaviour," CONCACAF said. "A comprehensive reckoning with this presidency is imperative." FIFA unveiled the plan on Tuesday, proposing a new commercial subsidiary, FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), to run the organisation's flagship events, including the World Cup and Club World Cup.

news.title: 'Nobody is selling football!' - FIFA responds to controversy and offers explanation after Gianni Infantino's World Cup plan sparks outrage
news.lede: FIFA has issued a firm response to the mounting backlash surrounding its controversial World Cup spin-off proposal, insisting that "nobody is selling football." The governing body claims media reports mischaracterised the plans and reaffirmed its commitment to a democratic process. FIFA has officially responded to the fierce opposition surrounding its proposed FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) project. The governing body released a public statement attempting to clear up what it described as "incorrect media reports" that disrupted the planned consultation process.

news.title: Gianni Infantino ‘has lost Uefa’s confidence’ after Fifa chief scraps World Cup sell-off plan
news.lede: Infantino ditched proposals after widespread backlash. Uefa adds: ‘We cannot keep going on with secret schemes’. Uefa has warned Gianni Infantino that his style of leadership cannot continue in demanding a thorough and fundamental review of Fifa’s governance. In a strongly worded statement that referred to “secret schemes”, “shabby backroom deals” and “faceless individuals”, the Uefa leadership made clear it wants change at the top of Fifa, despite the world governing body’s overnight U-turn in abandoning Infantino’s plan to sell off stakes in the World Cup and other competitions.

news.title: Gianni Infantino abandons plans to sell off stake in World Cup after widespread FIFA backlash
news.lede: FIFA president Gianni Infantino has abandoned his controversial plan to sell a stake in future World Cup profits to private equity investors after fierce opposition from football's governing bodies. But, despite walking back on his plans, UEFA has declared a loss of confidence in Infantino, with the Football Association supportive of the stance taken by European football's governing body. FIFA had announced on Tuesday that it was seeking to launch FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), which would bring together the sale of FIFA's commercial rights - including broadcasting, sponsorship, ticketing and licensing - with the operational delivery of its tournaments.
